response.sql: WITH type_counts AS (SELECT o.ordertune, COUNT(DISTINCT o.orderspivot) AS order_count FROM orderexecutions e JOIN orders o ON o.recordvault = e.ordersmark GROUP BY o.ordertune), shares AS (SELECT order_count, order_count::numeric / SUM(order_count) OVER () AS share FROM type_counts), compared AS (SELECT order_count, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS average_share FROM shares) SELECT SUM(order_count) AS total_order_count, AVG(share) AS average_share, AVG(share - average_share) AS average_excess_share FROM compared WHERE share > average_share;

assumptions.assumption: An executed order is counted once even if it has multiple execution records.

alternatives.interpretation: Count execution records by their order type, so an order with multiple executions contributes multiple times.
alternatives.sql: WITH type_counts AS (SELECT o.ordertune, COUNT(*) AS execution_count FROM orderexecutions e JOIN orders o ON o.recordvault = e.ordersmark GROUP BY o.ordertune), shares AS (SELECT execution_count, execution_count::numeric / SUM(execution_count) OVER () AS share FROM type_counts), compared AS (SELECT execution_count, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS average_share FROM shares) SELECT SUM(execution_count) AS total_execution_count, AVG(share) AS average_share, AVG(share - average_share) AS average_excess_share FROM compared WHERE share > average_share;
